title: Biweekly Quality Drift Briefing — Applied ML
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is the biweekly check-in summarizing observed quality drift and top failures across active model onboarding evals and prompt sets. It focuses on models currently in the onboarding pipeline (redwood-7b variants and 13b candidates), the primary prompt families we evaluate, and actionable next steps for engineering and applied ML.

Executive summary (2 minutes):
- Net regression rate across onboarding evals rose from 3.7% to 6.2% versus baseline over the past 14 days.
- Largest regressions concentrated in: short-form summarization prompts (onboard-shortform-v1) and FAQ/knowledge retrieval prompts (faq-rewrite-2026).
- Hallucination-related failures increased by ~180% in the faq-rewrite family relative to the prior period; false-positives in detection tasks rose modestly.
- Immediate actions: freeze redwood-13b-candidate rollout for production routing (JIRA:MLOPS-467), run targeted prompt augmentations, and schedule a model-kernel re-eval for redwood-7b-q4 (PR #981).

Key metrics (two-week window ending 2026-03-09):
- Total eval runs: 2,480 (all onboarding suites)
- Aggregate pass rate: 93.8% (was 96.3% two weeks prior)
- Mean task-level accuracy drop: -2.1 percentage points
- Top failure modes by count: hallucination (42%), omission (25%), formatting/regexp mismatch (18%), latency-induced truncation (15%)

Measurement notes:
- Evals run on eval-harness v2.3 against stable prompt seeds; prompt-randomization turned off for these drift checks.
- Baseline defined as the champion model snapshot when prompt_set was last signed off (see Confluence ONBOARD-EVALS-2026).
- Regression detection threshold: effect size >= 1.5% absolute change and p < 0.05 on bootstrap resampling.

Top failing prompt families (examples and diagnostics):
1) onboard-shortform-v1 (short bullet summarization)
   - Symptoms: brevity constraints violated; model expands into prose or omits key bullet items.
   - Example fail (expected bullets, got paragraph):
     Input: "Summarize this 4-line release note into three bullets: ..."
     Output: "The release includes updates to performance and security that improve stability across the platform and change some APIs..."
     Failure mode: omitted explicit list items, combined items into free text.
   - Metric impact: pass rate dropped from 95.6% to 88.2% on this family.
   - Potential cause: temperature defaults changed in serving runtime for redwood-7b-q4 (see PR #981), affecting deterministic output.

2) faq-rewrite-2026 (faq canonicalization + grounding)
   - Symptoms: confident but incorrect statements referencing non-existent feature flags; hallucinated links.
   - Example fail (hallucination):
     Input: "Does Redwood support per-request KMS encryption?"
     Expected: "No, we currently support workspace-level KMS; per-request KMS is on the roadmap (link to RFC)."
     Output: "Yes — enable per-request KMS in the console under Security -> Per-Request Keys."
   - Metric impact: hallucination failures rose from 4.0% to 11.3% for this set.
   - Potential cause: change in retrieval pipeline — cached KB snippets stale, and candidate reranker score thresholds were loosened last deploy (JIRA:MLOPS-452).

3) llm-formats (structured JSON response prompts)
   - Symptoms: extra trailing commas, null fields, or keys reordered causing downstream parsing errors.
   - Example fail: valid JSON required, but model emitted unquoted keys.
   - Metric impact: formatting regression contributed to 18% of total failures.
   - Potential cause: tokenizer update + prompt prefix rewording in prompt-template repo (see commit 2f9c).

Failure heatmap (high-level):
- redwood-7b-q4: most regressions in shortform and formats
- redwood-13b-candidate: stronger base accuracy on retrieval but higher hallucinations on out-of-domain KBs

Action items (owner -> task -> target date -> tracker):
- Marcus Li -> Pin redwood-13b-candidate routing to canary only; disable wide rollout -> 2026-03-12 -> JIRA:MLOPS-467
- Elena Park -> Re-run kb-cache-refresh and increase retriever recall threshold from 0.32->0.41 for faq-rewrite -> 2026-03-13 -> JIRA:MLOPS-452
- Ravi Menon -> Add structured-response postfix constraints and strict JSON validation in eval harness; create auto-failure tags on parse errors -> 2026-03-15 -> JIRA:MLOPS-474
- Samira Gomez -> Run controlled temperature sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.4) for redwood-7b-q4 on onboard-shortform-v1 and report sensitivity -> 2026-03-16 -> internal PR #1004
- Jordan Reyes -> Add 200 targeted adversarial prompts to faq-rewrite-2026 testing set (edge KBs) -> 2026-03-18 -> Confluence: ONBOARD-EVALS-2026#adversarial

Short-term hypotheses to validate (RACI notes):
- Hypothesis A (Elena/Ravi): Hallucinations rose because retriever returned stale KB passages; validating by replaying retrieval with fresh KB snapshot and comparing candidate ranks. If true: prioritize cache-refresh and tighten reranker threshold.
- Hypothesis B (Marcus/Samira): Determinism changes in serving (temperature defaults) increased variability for shortform prompts. Validate by comparing logits and sampling seeds across kernel versions. If true: revert default temp or supply explicit temp per-prompt.

Notes to reviewers / open questions:
- Do we prefer an emergency rollback of the PR that altered temperature defaults (PR #981) or a targeted per-prompt override? Rollback has broader stability implications.
- Are there contractual constraints for customer-owned KBs that prevent performing an immediate cache refresh? (security question for legal/ops).
- We observed one customer (acct: redwood-corp) with elevated failures — should we route their traffic to an older model snapshot while we mitigate?

Planned work for next 2 weeks:
- Add automated drift alerts for hallucination rate in the eval dashboard (threshold: 2x baseline or +5% abs).
- Expand prompt set coverage for shortform by +600 examples focused on list/bullet outputs.
- Integrate strict JSON schema validation step into pre-deploy gating.

Appendix A — quick links and artifacts: 
- Eval harness config: repo://eval-harness/configs/onboard-suite-2026.yaml
- PR to serving runtime: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/981
- Relevant Jira: MLOPS-452 (retriever thresholds), MLOPS-467 (candidate rollout), MLOPS-474 (eval parse failures)
- Confluence notes: https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/ONBOARD-EVALS-2026

Appendix B — sample diffs (short excerpts):
- redwood-7b-q4 vs baseline (shortform):
  baseline: "- Fixes bug X
- Improves perf
- Updates API"
  current: "The release includes fixes and performance improvements across the platform which improve stability and update APIs..."

If you want a deep-dive on any bullet above, list it in the Slack thread #applied-ml-regressions and tag @samira.

Document history:
- 2026-02-24: initial draft
- 2026-03-02: added shortform failure diagnostics and preliminary action list
- 2026-03-11: updated metrics, added hallucination analysis and final action owners

END OF BRIEFING
